from_quote: the President, with two thirds of the members present in the Senate, can make any treaty
rationale: The speaker says that under "this Constitution, the President, with two thirds of the members present in the Senate, can make any treaty", words close to those of Article II, Section 2, second clause.
to_quote: to make Treaties, provided two thirds of the Senators present concur

from_quote: to a speedy trial by an impartial jury of the vicinage, without whose unanimous consent he cannot be found guilty
rationale: The speaker says "Look at the bill of rights" and gives, partly in the text's words, its provision on trial by an impartial jury of the vicinage and unanimous consent; the words are not in quotation marks, and the words before them are not the text's.
to_quote: to a ſpeedy trial by an impartial jury of his vicinage, whithout whoſe unanimous conſent he cannot be found guilty

from_quote: all men are by nature free and independent
rationale: The speaker says "Our declaration of rights tells us" and quotes "all men are by nature free and independent," with "&c." after it; the text has "equally" before "free".
to_quote: all men are by nature equally free and independent

from_quote: but in consequence of appropriations made by law
rationale: The speaker says the congressional proceedings are to be published, including all receipts and expenditures of public money, "of which no part can be used but in consequence of appropriations made by law"; Article I, Section 9, seventh clause has "but in Consequence of Appropriations made by Law".
to_quote: but in Consequence of Appropriations made by Law

from_quote: The exclusive power of legislation over the ten miles square
rationale: The speaker refers to "The exclusive power of legislation over the ten miles square".
to_quote: exercise exclusive Legislation in all Cases whatsoever, over such District (not exceeding ten Miles square)
